details: Recent diffusion language models (DLMs) share common components (masked diffusion, block diffusion, fast decoding), but these live in ad-hoc, opaque codebases with inconsistent training/inference/evaluation interfaces, making reproduction, fair comparison, and extension hard.

dLLM: an open-source framework unifying the end-to-end DLM pipeline around three modular components — Trainer (MDLM and BD3LM objectives, plus an EditFlow reference), a plug-and-play Sampler abstraction that decouples inference algorithms from model implementations, and a unified evaluation interface extending lm-evaluation-harness.

Key design principle: diffusion-modeling logic is decoupled from model architecture and built as thin wrappers on the HuggingFace stack, so pretraining, SFT, block diffusion, and AR-to-diffusion adaptation differ only by a trainer swap or small config/collator changes.
Accompanying artifact: minimal, reproducible recipes and released checkpoints for converting off-the-shelf BERT-style encoders and autoregressive LMs into small DLMs.
MDLMTrainer and BD3LMTrainer wrapping transformers Trainer; accelerate/FSDP/DeepSpeed for scaling, peft for LoRA.
Sampler API: MDLMSampler and drop-in MDLMFastdLLMSampler implementing Fast-dLLM's block-wise approximate KV cache and confidence-based parallel decoding.
Terminal visualizer exposing token decoding order and sample evolution over steps.
Evaluation built on lm-evaluation-harness with per-model/per-task matching of preprocessing, decoding settings, and post-processing to official pipelines.
LLaDA (Base/Instruct, 8B) and Dream (Base/Instruct, 7B) finetuned with MDLM SFT + LoRA (r=128, alpha=256) on s1K, loss on response tokens only.
Seq len 4096, 20 epochs, lr 1e-5, global batch 32, cosine schedule with 10% warmup, 8xA100 with DeepSpeed ZeRO-2; <reasoning> token prepended at inference; evaluation pipelines from d1.
Benchmarks: GSM8K, MATH500, Countdown, Sudoku, HumanEval, MBPP.
ModernBERT-base/large finetuned with MDLM SFT only (no continual pretraining, no architecture change) on Tulu 3 SFT + SmolTalk.
Seq len 1024, 10 epochs, lr 1e-4, global batch 384, bf16, cosine + 10% warmup, 8xA100 ZeRO-2.
Compared against GPT-2/GPT-2-medium (evaluated with dLLM) and reported Qwen1.5-0.5B / -Chat numbers on GSM8K, BBH, MATH, MMLU, HellaSwag, LAMBADA, WinoGrande.
Qwen3-0.6B backbone tuned with SFT only under MDLM (seq 1024) and BD3LM (seq 512, block size 32) on Tulu 3 SFT + SmolTalk + opc-sft-stage1&2.
10 epochs, lr 1e-4, global batch 2048, bf16, cosine schedule, 64xA100 ZeRO-2; logits right-shifting trick from prior work deliberately omitted (hurt performance in their experiments).
Compared to reported Qwen2.5-0.5B and Qwen3-0.6B-Base numbers on GSM8K, BBH, MATH, MMLU(-Pro), HellaSwag, HumanEval, MBPP.

Reproduction of official LLaDA and Dream (Base/Instruct) scores across ~11 benchmarks, and of Fast-dLLM accuracy/throughput with max new tokens 256 and 512 under Cache, Parallel, and combined settings.
Hyperparameter sensitivity sweeps varying EOS suppression, CFG=0.5, parallel decoding of 4 tokens/step, and temperature=0.

key_findings.finding: Off-the-shelf pretrained non-diffusion backbones can be converted into functional DLM chatbots with only lightweight SFT, no architectural change and no continual pretraining.
key_findings.evidence: ModernBERT-large-chat, trained purely with MDLM SFT on instruction data, beats both GPT-2 variants on most of GSM8K/BBH/MATH/MMLU/HellaSwag and exceeds Qwen1.5-0.5B-Chat on BBH (25.6 vs 18.2) and MATH (3.6 vs 2.1); Qwen3-0.6B converted with BD3LM SFT reaches HumanEval 46.3 and MBPP 38.2, above Qwen3-0.6B-Base (32.3 / 36.6), though still trailing on MMLU and BBH.

key_findings.finding: DLM benchmark results are highly sensitive to inference hyperparameters, a fragility rarely made explicit in prior work.
key_findings.evidence: Sweeps on LLaDA-Instruct and Dream-Instruct show sharp degradation from the best configuration when changing a single knob (no EOS suppression, cfg=0.5, 4 tokens/step parallel decoding, temperature=0); Fast-dLLM numbers also shift with max new tokens (256 vs 512), which changes pre-allocated padding in the bidirectional window.

key_findings.finding: The unified evaluation pipeline reproduces officially reported scores for major open-weight DLMs and for Fast-dLLM speedups.
key_findings.evidence: LLaDA-Base and Dream-Base reproductions match official numbers closely across MMLU/BBH/ARC-C/GSM8K/MATH/HumanEval/MBPP (e.g., LLaDA-Base MMLU 65.9 vs 65.9, Dream-Base GSM8K 77.0 vs 77.2); the dLLM Fast-dLLM sampler achieves comparable accuracy with large throughput gains (e.g., LLaDA-Instruct GSM8K@256 6.5x with cache+parallel vs 8.1x official).

key_findings.finding: MDLM-style SFT on reasoning data reliably improves instruction-tuned DLMs but generalizes poorly when applied to base DLMs.
key_findings.evidence: s1K LoRA SFT lifts LLaDA-Instruct on all six benchmarks (e.g., Countdown 19.92→26.95) and Dream-Instruct on most (Sudoku 6.93→19.68), while base models gain on in-distribution math (LLaDA-Base GSM8K 64.67→73.62) but regress out of distribution (HumanEval 25.00→18.90, MBPP 40.08→28.79).

key_findings.finding: A single modular interface suffices to span the main DLM training regimes, requiring only localized configuration edits.
key_findings.evidence: MDLM pretraining becomes BD3LM pretraining by swapping MDLMTrainer for BD3LMTrainer; SFT requires only a NoAttentionMaskWrapper plus label_pad_token_id=eos; AR-to-MDLM adaptation requires only right_shift_logits and a PrependBOSWrapper — and all reported recipes (LLaDA/Dream SFT, BERT-Chat, Tiny-A2D) were produced through this same interface.
